findings.title: Project Funding Sandwich Attack
findings.cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization
findings.description: Project funding creates a timing window where attackers can front-run or back-run funding transactions to claim the most valuable indices. The fundProject function immediately makes indices available after funding, enabling MEV extraction through strategic index claiming.
findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Attacker monitors mempool for fundProject transactions
2. Front-runs funding with claimToContribute calls to grab indices 0-N
3. Forces legitimate contributors to claim suboptimal indices
4. Originators pay premium for 'good' indices, attacker profits from index arbitrage
findings.economic_impact: Originators pay MEV tax for project funding, index values become speculative, protocol loses efficiency
mitigation_suggestions: Implement commit-reveal for index claiming
Add random index assignment with post-reveal shuffling
Use VRF for index randomization
Add funding cooldown period before indices become claimable

findings.title: Consensus Oracle Manipulation via Sybil Coordination
findings.description: Consensus algorithm uses sqrt(stake) * reputation weighting, enabling coordinated Sybil attacks where multiple low-stake accounts can manipulate consensus outcomes. The sqrt weighting amplifies the impact of small coordinated stakes.

evidence_locations.code:
uint256 internal constant TIER_1_SLASH_BPS = 1000; // 10%
uint256 internal constant TIER_2_SLASH_BPS = 2500; // 25%
uint256 internal constant TIER_3_SLASH_BPS = 5000; // 50%
uint256 internal constant TIER_4_SLASH_BPS = 10000; // 100%

findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Attacker creates 10 accounts with minimum stake (e.g., 100 tokens each)
2. Each account commits identical manipulated scores
3. sqrt(100) * 1000 = 1000 weight per account, total 10k weight
4. Coordinated attack overwhelms honest validators with 10:1 weight ratio
5. Consensus manipulated despite slashing risk being distributed across accounts
findings.economic_impact: Consensus becomes unreliable, high-quality contributions rejected, low-quality work accepted, reputation system corrupted
mitigation_suggestions: Implement quadratic staking (stake² weighting instead of sqrt(stake))
Add minimum stake thresholds that scale with project size
Implement cross-validation correlation checks
Add reputation decay for coordinated voting patterns

findings.title: Free Option via Ghost Validator Commitments
findings.description: Validators can commit to validations without revealing, creating free options. They can observe consensus outcomes and only reveal if it benefits them, while committed stake remains locked but non-performing.

evidence_locations.code:
if (vc.settled) revert IQualityEngine.AlreadySettled();
if (vc.revealedAt == 0) revert IQualityEngine.NotCommitted();

findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Validator commits with minimum stake during commit window
2. Observes other validators' reveals and emerging consensus
3. If consensus favors revealing: reveal and collect rewards
4. If consensus opposes revealing: don't reveal, wait for slash (free option)
5. Stake loss is bounded, potential reward is unbounded
findings.economic_impact: Validators become risk-free, consensus participation drops, economic security degrades, protocol becomes manipulable by remaining participants
mitigation_suggestions: Implement forced reveal mechanism with time-based randomization
Add reputation penalties for non-reveal even without slashing
Reduce commit windows and increase reveal requirements
Implement probabilistic slashing for non-participation

findings.title: Dispute Griefing via Bond Arbitrage
findings.description: Disputes can be opened with minimal bonds to grief contributors and delay reward release. The dispute bond calculation uses rewardRate * disputeBondBps, but bond is returned if dispute is rejected, creating low-risk griefing opportunities.
findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Attacker monitors accepted contributions
2. Opens frivolous disputes with minimum bond during challenge window
3. Extends challenge period, delaying contributor rewards
4. Dispute gets rejected, bond returned, contributor reward delayed
5. Repeat across multiple indices for maximum grief
findings.economic_impact: Contributors suffer delayed rewards and opportunity costs, dispute mechanism abused for harassment, protocol UX degraded
mitigation_suggestions: Increase dispute bond scaling with project value
Implement dispute reputation system with escalating bonds
Add dispute pre-screening requirements
Limit concurrent disputes per challenger

findings.title: Reputation Farming via Flash Projects
findings.description: Attackers can create flash-funded projects, contribute their own work, validate it positively, and extract reputation gains before abandoning the project. The phased settlement allows reputation extraction without economic commitment.

evidence_locations.code:
ReputationLib.update(msg.sender, C.ORIGINATOR_ROLE_KEY, true, 0);
emit IQualityEngine.ProjectCreated(projectId, msg.sender);

findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Create project with minimal funding
2. Claim and contribute own work
3. Create multiple validator accounts to validate positively
4. Achieve consensus, extract reputation boost
5. Abandon project without completing settlement
6. Repeat with new accounts for reputation farming
findings.economic_impact: Reputation inflation undermines trust system, legitimate participants disadvantaged, consensus quality degrades
mitigation_suggestions: Require minimum project duration before reputation extraction
Implement reputation stake-locking
Add reputation decay for inactive accounts
Require minimum project completion rates for reputation maintenance

findings.title: Fee Rounding Bias in Multi-Fee Waterfall
findings.cwe: CWE-1339: Insufficient Precision or Accuracy of a Real Number
findings.description: Multiple sequential fee deductions (protocol, origination adapter, contribution adapter, validation adapter) create cumulative rounding bias. Each fee uses integer division, systematically favoring the protocol treasury over adapters and participants.
findings.exploit_scenario: Small reward amounts get progressively rounded down through each fee tier. A 100 token reward with 2% fees each becomes: 100 → 98 (protocol) → 96.04 (adapter) → 94.12 (final), with fractions lost to rounding.
findings.economic_impact: Adapters receive less than expected fees, participants receive less rewards, protocol treasury benefits from accumulated rounding dust
mitigation_suggestions: Use higher precision arithmetic (e.g., 1e18 scaling)
Reverse fee order (deduct smallest fees first)
Accumulate rounding dust and redistribute periodically
Use fee ceiling functions instead of floor

findings.title: Validator Reward Dilution via Capacity Gaming
findings.description: Validators can game capacity allocation to maximize reward dilution. By committing maximum capacity but selectively revealing only for profitable validations, validators create asymmetric reward opportunities while maintaining capacity for other opportunities.
findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Validator locks large capacity across multiple projects
2. Monitors emerging consensus across all commitments
3. Selectively reveals only in validations where they can be 'accurate' (follow majority)
4. Non-revealed commitments eventually get slashed or expire
5. Rewards concentrated on profitable reveals, losses distributed across non-profitable commitments
findings.economic_impact: Validator rewards become lottery-like, consensus quality depends on selective participation, economic security becomes uneven
mitigation_suggestions: Implement capacity commitment penalties for non-participation
Add reputation penalties for selective revealing patterns
Require minimum participation rates for capacity maintenance
Implement capacity utilization tracking with rewards

findings.title: Originator Stake Timing Attack
findings.description: Originators can manipulate project funding timing to avoid stake requirements. By funding projects when originatorStakeRequirement is 0, then changing requirements, or using flash loans to temporarily meet requirements.

evidence_locations.code:
// Default dispute configuration (packed in slot 1 and slot 3)
$.disputeBondBps = 1000; // 10% of rewardRate
$.originatorReportBondBps = 100; // 1% of totalRewards
$.originatorStakeRequirement = 0; // disabled by default

findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Originator monitors for favorable market conditions
2. Funds project when stake requirement is temporarily 0
3. Immediately contributes low-quality work
4. Originates disputes or reports to extract value without accountability
5. Abandons project before stake requirements change
findings.economic_impact: Originators can bypass accountability mechanisms, protocol loses economic security through unenforced originator stakes
mitigation_suggestions: Make stake requirements fixed at project creation time
Implement minimum stake requirement periods
Add stake requirement voting mechanisms
Use time-weighted stake requirements

findings.title: Consensus Flash Loan Manipulation
findings.cwe: CWE-366: Race Condition within a Thread
findings.description: Flash loans can be used to temporarily inflate validator capacity for consensus manipulation. Borrowed stake can be committed to swing consensus outcomes, then returned before settlement, avoiding slashing penalties.
findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Attacker takes flash loan of large stake amount
2. Sets validator capacity with borrowed stake
3. Commits to validation with manipulated score
4. If successful, consensus manipulated without permanent stake loss
5. If caught as outlier, slash amount limited to borrowed stake
6. Return flash loan before settlement completes
findings.economic_impact: Consensus becomes flash-loan resistant but economically insecure, large stakeholders can manipulate outcomes with temporary capital
mitigation_suggestions: Implement stake commitment lock periods
Add stake age requirements for validation weight
Use time-averaged stake calculations
Implement flash loan detection mechanisms

findings.title: Reward Claiming Gas Griefing
findings.description: Universal claimReward function allows griefing by repeatedly claiming zero amounts or using gas-intensive token transfers. While economically neutral, this creates UX friction and potential gas exhaustion attacks.
findings.exploit_scenario:
1. Attacker repeatedly calls claimReward with zero balance
2. Each call consumes gas and emits events
3. Creates noise in protocol monitoring systems
4. Could be combined with fee-on-transfer tokens for gas exhaustion
5. Forces legitimate users to pay higher gas costs
findings.economic_impact: Increased gas costs for legitimate users, degraded UX, potential network congestion during high activity periods
mitigation_suggestions: Add minimum claim thresholds
Implement batched claiming mechanisms
Add claim cooldown periods
Use more efficient storage patterns
